exceptions.justification: Lints commit messages against Conventional Commits (via @commitlint/cli, a real dependency) using only a read-only `git log` range -- never writes to the consumer's repo.

Reads the merged coverage artifact this package's own Tests/Coverage checks already produced and reports CRAP (complexity x uncovered-risk) per function -- a real dependency, read-only, no network access.
dependency-cruiser statically analyzes the consumer's own import graph against the bundled/consumer-supplied rule config -- a real dependency, read-only, no network access.
Lints the consumer's own .github/workflows/*.yml for correctness/security issues -- a real dependency (github-actionlint), read-only, no network access.
jscpd detects copy-pasted code blocks in the consumer's own src/ -- a real dependency, read-only, no network access.

knip finds unused files/exports/dependencies via static analysis of the consumer's own source and package.json -- a real dependency, read-only (does not modify package.json itself), no network access.
Lints the consumer's own root and docs/ Markdown against the bundled/consumer-supplied rule config -- a real dependency, read-only, no network access.

Spawns this package's own bundled scripts/*.mjs (e.g. run-generated.mjs, check-suppressions.mjs) via the Node binary already running the contract itself -- not a third-party tool; every script it can spawn ships in this package's own `files` allowlist and is reviewed as ordinary source, not as an external command.

Runs one of the consumer's own package.json scripts (npm run <script>) -- npm itself ships with Node, and the script it invokes is the consumer's own, already-reviewed code, not a third-party command this package introduces.
secretlint scans the consumer's own tracked files for accidentally-committed secrets against the bundled/consumer-supplied rule config -- a real dependency, read-only, no network access.

Socket.dev's own CLI (@socketsecurity/cli, a real dependency) scans the consumer's dependency tree for supply-chain risk; only runs (and only ever makes network calls) when the consumer has installed and authenticated it themselves -- SecuritySocket's own policy already treats an unauthenticated/not-installed environment as a warn, never a silent skip.

Runs the consumer's own test suite -- a real dependency, the standard way every check in this package (and every consumer) already runs tests; no network access beyond whatever the consumer's own tests themselves make.
